meta.note: Evidence-Gap Register entries of the FX part; also written as GOVERNANCE/register/EG-FX-nn.md

gaps.title: Wheatfield fire
gaps.description: No documented wheat-field fire; S-033 uses "fire" for gunfire (forum citing Pfanz, low reliability).
gaps.substitute: Not drawn. Trampling is the structures layer's business.

gaps.title: Rogers house, Schmucker Hall, other buildings burned
gaps.description: Only fires documented in the repository are built (Sherfy barn, Bliss house and barn, Rock Creek trestle, rail cars at the station, carcass fires). Rogers, Schmucker and the McPherson barn did not burn (rule RULE-01).

gaps.title: Caledonia Furnace and the Gettysburg covered bridge
gaps.description: Furnace: burned by Early's division on June 26, 1863 per the Pennsylvania state historical marker (ExplorePAHistory marker 1-A-1DE, dedicated 1947, at US 30 and PA 233, Caledonia State Park, east of Fayetteville, FRANKLIN County; secondary, so inferred, not documented); Early's own OR reports do not mention it (T1-005 NOT_FOUND_IN_OR). The site is in Franklin County, so the plan's "about 2 miles out on the Cashtown road" is not supported by the marker and the furnace lies off the loaded terrain. Bridge: Early's OR report (printed p. 465) says a "small railroad bridge near the place" was burned with the 10 or 12 cars; the OR does not call it covered (T1-014, T1-015), so "covered" is a plan-row claim with no supporting source. The structures data has a point for the Rock Creek trestle (fx-fire-rock-creek-trestle, T1-016, sources vary 26 or 27 June); that it is the bridge Early's report means is an inference (the OR gives no name), and no survey position exists for the furnace buildings.
gaps.substitute: Furnace not drawn (off terrain, county-level location only). Bridge drawn only as the marked Rock Creek trestle fire; the word "covered" is not used for it.

gaps.title: Bursting charge of common shell and spherical case
gaps.description: CLOSED for the 12-pdr, 24-pdr and 32-pdr smoothbore shell (Hand-book of Artillery, Richmond 1861, p. 108: to burst 5, 8 and 11 oz) and for spherical case (6-pdr 2.5, 12-pdr 4.5, 24-pdr 6, 32-pdr 8 oz; Ordnance Manual 1861 p. 256 and Roberts p. 108). The 1.0 oz case charge read earlier from the OCR of Instruction for Field Artillery 1863 p. 13 (76 balls) conflicts with both and is kept as the selectable scenario fa1863_ocr (PENDING OWNER). STILL OPEN: the 6-pdr shell, the mountain howitzer and all rifled shells (no printed table reached).
gaps.substitute: Table values by designation; rifled and 6-pdr shells use the 12-pdr value (plausible-procedural stand-in), marked.

gaps.title: Canister cone angle and ground-strike pattern
gaps.description: Gibbon 1860 (Practice of fire, printed p. 268-269): canister and grape leave the piece in a cone, most balls near the centre, the extreme ones separating about one tenth of the range; good results at 300-600 yd, maximum effect 400-450 yd. The width is documented; reading it as the full width (half-angle 2.86 degrees) rather than as each extreme ball one tenth off the axis (5.71 degrees) is inferred, so both readings are carried (choices.canisterSpread). The density profile inside the cone and the ground-strike pattern are not described (Gibbon: most balls near the centre).
gaps.substitute: Half-angle 2.86 degrees (inferred) by default, 5.71 degrees as the alternative; lateral sigma = half width / 2 (plausible-procedural look parameter).

gaps.title: Smoke, dust and flame physics of 1863
gaps.description: The PDF supplies no measured smoke yield, extinction, plume rise, flame length or dust yield; T2-122 is itself plausible-procedural ("sector-by-sector smoke accounts were not found").
gaps.substitute: Physically coherent look parameters, every one tier-marked in TIERS.json; the benchmark is the plan's G12 band (flash 80-150 ms, plume 15-25 s, dirt column 10-25 m).

gaps.title: March cadence and dust accounts
gaps.description: CLOSED for infantry cadence: Hardee prints common time 90, quick time 110, route step 110, double quick 165 and 180 under urgent need (verified in the OCR of three Hardee editions in tmp/library/misc), now a documented table used when a unit_march event gives no stepsPerMin. STILL OPEN: the PDF says "no direct dust accounts" (the dust yield stays a look parameter), and the cadence of horse gaits is not documented (the printed paces of 1861-63 give speeds only, e.g. Wheeler 1863 p. 87: walk 3.75, trot 7.5, gallop 10 mph; Cooper 1861 p. 7; Instruction for Field Artillery 1863 p. 47: 400 yd in 4.5, 2 and 1 minute; see app/data/anim3d/gait-sources.json; none prints a hoof or stride rate, so strikes per minute stay a look parameter).
gaps.substitute: Dust drawn only when the ground is dry by the wetness model; horse strikes per minute stay plausible-procedural.

gaps.title: Fire timing inside date-only windows, and burn durations
gaps.description: Sherfy barn (Jul 2 evening to Jul 3 afternoon), Bliss (Jul 3 morning), trestle (Jun 26 or 27): the part of the day is not recorded; no burn duration is recorded for any building.
gaps.substitute: Fire drawn at half intensity and marked "time uncertain" inside the window; growth, peak and decline times are plausible-procedural. The owner picks a scenario or a clock (PENDING OWNER).

gaps.title: Wind speed and direction
gaps.description: Speed conflict 2 vs 12 mph (CF-WIND-SPEED, PENDING OWNER); direction not recorded for Jun 26-30 and Jul 4; "no breeze during the Charge" is qualitative.
gaps.substitute: The effects follow the environment layer's chosen scenario; unrecorded days use S-SSW and are flagged; Jul 3 13:00-16:30 wind scaled by params.wind.calm_charge_scale.

gaps.title: Powder charge of small arms other than the .58 rifle-musket; charges of rifled field guns and gap pieces
gaps.description: Only the 60-grain rifled-musket charge and the smoothbore field-gun and howitzer service charges are in printed manuals in the repository. Lookups of this round that found nothing: Ordnance Manual 3rd ed. 1862 OCR (archive.org ordnancemanualfo00unitrich): no Parrott, no 3-inch rifle service charge, no small-arms cartridge powder weight reached by the patterns tried; Roberts 1861 has no rifled field gun. Gibbon 1860 prints 60 grains of powder for the rifled musket at 200 and 600 yd (already used). PARTLY CLOSED (vis-fx round 2): Instruction for Field Artillery (adopted 1863-03-03, New York 1864, printed p. 7 note) prints one pound for the 10-pounder Parrott and the 3-inch gun and two pounds for the 20-pounder Parrott, now documented. STILL OPEN: the 14-pdr James, 12-pdr Whitworth, Blakely, 3-inch navy rifle and Ames rifled bronze piece (no printed charge reached) and every small arm other than the .58 rifle-musket.
gaps.substitute: Other arms scaled by bore area from the documented 60 grains (plausible-procedural); the 14-pdr James and Whitworth use the kit table (inferred, weak source); Blakely, navy rifle and Ames use a 1.0 lb stand-in (plausible-procedural).

gaps.title: Muzzle-flash jet length and duration per weapon
gaps.description: Only the project's own estimates exist (audio/contract/FIRE_EVENT.md section 3; render G12): "tens of ms", "several metres", "50-100 ms" and "80-150 ms".
gaps.substitute: Jet length L = k * cbrt(charge) with k fitted to those words; duration carried as the union range.

gaps.title: Fuse trails at night
gaps.description: The plan lists fuse trails as a night light source (T2-203) and marks it plausible-procedural ("no night-light accounts were found").
gaps.substitute: Drawn for timed-fuze projectiles only (shell, spherical case), never for solid shot, canister or percussion rifled shell; marked.

gaps.title: Horse-carcass fires: where and until when
gaps.description: 3,000-5,000 horses burned with kerosene "where possible" from Jul 4 (T3-150); no positions, no end.
gaps.substitute: Host places them; window starts Jul 4 00:00 (date only); marked.

gaps.title: Burning fence rails
gaps.description: Leister rails burned (S-059), Thompson fences burned for firewood (T3-067): cause and extent unrecorded.

gaps.title: Camp-fire positions
gaps.description: Rear camp fires are plausible-procedural in the PDF; no positions recorded.
gaps.substitute: Host-placed; refused within params.fire.campfire.contact_clearance_m of an enemy or a firing line.

gaps.title: Nothing seen
gaps.description: Software rendering only (SwiftShader, this machine has no GPU). The WebGL2 and WebGPU shader code compiles and draws on the software adapters, with no compiler message or validation error on WebGPU, the two APIs agree to within 0.46 of 255 (mean absolute), and the pictures were looked at (2026-11-13, app/docs/WEATHER3D-WEBGPU-NOTES.md). The look, the performance and the lighting on a real GPU are unverified, and the GPU-cull compute shader is not wired or compared with the CPU cull.
